items.summary: Aleksandar Vučić, leader of the Serbian Progressive Party and former president, conceded that the Student List won Serbia's parliamentary election. Framed as a referendum on his decade-plus dominance, he said preliminary results give the movement 135 to 140 seats—enough for a majority—and around 2.2 million votes (52%), versus roughly 1.72 million (32.3%) for his party. He called it a new political era; coverage notes the story is developing.
items.title: Serbian President Concedes Student List Victory in Parliamentary Election

items.summary: As Australia's parliament resumed, independent MP Helen Haines was honoured after being struck by a vehicle in Wangaratta on 19 October. Colleagues signed a civility pledge she began before the alleged attack, while Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of doing justice to her legacy.
items.title: Australia politics live: MPs to pay tribute to Helen Haines as parliament resumes; Hanson says One Nation cartoons ‘not going anywhere’

items.summary: A five-year-old Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby, died in Alice Springs; her body was found in late April. A long-awaited review of the Department of Children and Families' handling of notifications about her life prompted intense media attention after confidential information leaked to journalists. The report identified family and domestic violence by her father as the main risk and recorded 14 notifications since 2020, five before her death. It made 45 recommendations, which the government has accepted but some question will bring real change.
items.title: NT child protection review exposes domestic violence failures after girl's death

items.summary: Forty students competed in the ninth edition of the 2026 Bournda Bird Olympics, held in Merimbula on the NSW far south coast. Competitors mimicked native Australian birds over an hour while judges considered accuracy and creativity. Tathra Public School won; judge Bob Harris said it fosters interest in nature.
items.title: Forty students revive bird calling at Bournda Bird Olympics

items.summary: A cabinet split has emerged over whether to approve drilling at the controversial North Sea Rosebank oilfield, with chancellor John Healey in favour and energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh leaning toward rejection. A final decision is expected before year end; if rejected, it would be a blow for the industry but a victory for climate campaigners.
items.title: Cabinet split over Rosebank oilfield drilling approval

items.summary: Bill Ackman, founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, said on Sunday that Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel's next government. He argued their exclusion would signal Israel was 'turning a new page' after they caused what he called enormous reputational damage. The statement came two days before the election, which polls show is tight between Netanyahu's coalition and opposition parties.
items.title: Ackman Opposes Ben-Gvir and Smotrich in Next Israeli Cabinet

items.summary: A May 15 concert in San Diego featuring singer Pink raised $8.25 million for cancer research through Curebound, a San Diego-based organisation supporting cancer research. The event drew around 25,000 attendees at Petco Park and marked the latest contribution to the Concert for Cures series, which has collected more than $28 million across four concerts since 2022. Pink spoke about gratitude toward those involved in the cause.
items.title: Pink's San Diego cancer benefit raises $8.25m, taking series past $28m

items.summary: This piece argues that strong communication skills and a calm, collected mind are essential for handling any situation well. It explains that steering conversation is a balancing act: one must listen while also sharing views skillfully, since neither pure listening nor talking without giving others a chance makes communication effective. A Vedic couplet advises to speak the truth pleasantly but not an unpleasant truth or pleasant lie, and regular meditation helps find the right way to express oneself.
items.title: Guiding Light: Art Of Effective Communication

items.summary: A New York appeals court reversed a lower-court foreclosure ruling after US Bank National Association failed to prove its right to enforce the loan. Moses Sukljian, who signed a 2005 mortgage in Albany County, argued the bank could not establish standing because key documents were undated and absent from the original complaint. The two allonges it later produced lacked dates and prior inclusion, so judgment for the bank was vacated without a trial.
items.title: Appeals Court Reverses Foreclosure Ruling Over Missing Loan Documents

items.summary: Sudden downpours and localised flooding can leave motorists facing unexpected repair bills even outside the traditional monsoon season. As weather patterns become increasingly unpredictable, car owners need to understand what their motor insurance covers and whether additional protection is necessary. For a 34-year-old software engineer commuting through Bengaluru, heavy rain can turn familiar roads into waterlogged stretches. If the car stalls in floodwater and requires towing and repairs, costs could depend significantly on the policy and add-ons purchased.
items.title: Motor Insurance Add-Ons for Flood and Sudden Rain Damage

items.summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said information technology has become a core function of the central bank, with sovereign data centres and cybersecurity capabilities critical to financial-system resilience as artificial intelligence reshapes technology. The remarks followed an interview with Doordarshan after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated RBI's new data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar.
items.title: RBI Governor Says Data Centres Must Stay Sovereign Amid AI Shift

items.summary: Three months after Elon Musk promised a full-length, historically accurate film version of The Odyssey, Grok released only seven minutes, now called Episode 1 of the series. Created with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker, the footage drew comparison to Nolan's practical-effects epic. The author found it less ugly than expected but lacking artistry, inspiration, human interest, momentum, and Musk-approved skin colors.
items.title: Grok Releases Seven Minutes of AI Odyssey

items.summary: An RBI study published in the RBI Bulletin finds that banks pass interest-rate hikes through contract repricing more completely than cuts, transmitting 76.4% of a tightening but only 64% of an easing between early 2025 and March 2026. Researchers Yuvraj Kashyap, Kamal Gupta and Arvind Jha say banks protect net interest margins during rate falls by widening spreads or shifting toward higher-yielding loans.
items.title: RBI Study Finds Banks Pass Rate Hikes Faster Than Cuts

items.summary: In askST Jobs, business correspondent Timothy Goh addresses a reader asking why colleagues receive more family-related work flexibility than they do. HR director Don Leow of the National Institute of Education says bosses should not assume childless staff have fewer outside responsibilities and that fairness means treating legitimate needs fairly without repeatedly burdening dependable employees. Senior manager Allie Teh at Robert Walters Singapore adds workplace support should be reciprocal within reasonable limits.
items.title: Singapore experts weigh in on fair workplace flexibility

items.summary: Second-generation business leader Yeo Zong Han joined UOB Private Bank’s sixth run of its Next Generation Programme, travelling from Aug 31 to Sept 4 in Shanghai and Hangzhou. Along with 25 individuals aged 20 to 37 from seven markets, he met leaders from companies such as Unitree Robotics, Ant Group, Jinko Power, YX Digital and Semir Group. The programme, launched in 2020, focuses on curiosity, leadership potential and openness rather than family background alone. Participants like Kristen Geng said it deepened their understanding of intergenerational wealth transfer. UOB Private Bank head Chew Mun Yew noted urgency to groom successors as many clients are first-generation wealth creators. The trip included a stop at the China Europe International Business School Centre for Family Heritage, with participants describing it as rest and learning rather than pure relaxation.
items.title: UOB’s Next-Generation Programme Sends Heirs to China
